# Data Schema

## Input (generated by `data/generate_transactions.py`)

### `data/synthetic/customers.csv`

| column | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| customer_id | string | `C0000`..`C0599`, zero-padded, sorted ascending |
| signup_day | int | day-offset from EPOCH (2024-01-01) the customer signed up |

### `data/synthetic/transactions.csv`

| column | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| customer_id | string | foreign key into customers.csv |
| order_index | int | 0-based position of this transaction within the customer's own history, sorted by day_offset (deterministic tie-break) |
| day_offset | int | day-offset from EPOCH the transaction occurred |
| event | string | product category code, one of `A`,`B`,`C`,`D`,`E` |
| amount_cents | int | transaction amount in integer cents (avoids floating point) |

Dates are derived as `EPOCH + timedelta(days=day_offset)` (see `mining/util.py:day_to_date`). EPOCH is a fixed constant, not read from the system clock, which is what keeps output deterministic.

## Output (`sample_output/`, written by `run_demo.py`)

### `mining_report.md`

Human-readable Markdown report: dataset summary, frequent sequential patterns, per-cohort retention tables, churn associations table, and a Limitations section. See the file itself for the exact layout.

### `sequences.csv`

| column | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| length | int | pattern length (1, 2, or 3) |
| pattern | string | ordered pattern rendered as `"A -> B"` |
| support_customers | int | number of distinct customers whose history contains this ordered subsequence |

Sorted by descending support, then pattern (lexicographic) for determinism.

### `churn_associations.csv`

| column | type | description |
|---|---|---|
| group_label | string | the trait being tested, e.g. `sequence A -> B`, `frequency bucket = low` |
| support_count | int | number of customers with the trait |
| n_total_customers | int | total customers in the dataset |
| n_with_trait | int | customers with the trait (== support_count) |
| churned_with_trait | int | of those, how many are labeled churned |
| churn_rate_with | float | churned_with_trait / n_with_trait |
| churn_rate_with_wilson_lower / _upper | float | 95% Wilson score interval bounds for churn_rate_with |
| n_without_trait | int | customers without the trait |
| churned_without_trait | int | of those, how many are labeled churned |
| churn_rate_without | float | churned_without_trait / n_without_trait |
| churn_rate_without_wilson_lower / _upper | float | 95% Wilson score interval bounds for churn_rate_without |
| lift | float or "n/a" | churn_rate_with / churn_rate_without; "n/a" when the baseline rate is 0 |
| note | string | fixed correlational-not-causal disclaimer, present on every row |

Sorted by descending lift (rows with undefined/`n/a` lift sort last), then group_label.

### `run_summary.txt`

Plain-text key:value run parameters and headline counts (customer/transaction counts, cutoff day, churn window, min support threshold, counts of churned customers, patterns found, associations reported). No wall-clock timestamp is included, by design, so the file is reproducible byte-for-byte.

## Internal (in-memory) representations

* `mining.util.Customer(customer_id, signup_day)`
* `mining.util.Transaction(customer_id, order_index, day_offset, event, amount_cents)`
* `mining.churn.AssociationResult` — see `mining/churn.py` for the full field list; mirrors the churn_associations.csv columns above plus a `mining.stats.WilsonInterval` object per side.
